Bram Stoker, Dracula.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/bram-stoker/dracula

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Bram Stoker, the author, the dedicatee, the writer of a preface, died 1912 (Wikidata Q36184, P570 = 1912-04-20).

First publication of the text used: 1897 (SE colophon: 'Dracula was published in 1897 by Bram Stoker.').

Why this is public domain:
- United States: Standard Ebooks states that the text is in the United States public domain (rights statement below).
- Country of origin (United Kingdom): the text was first published there in May 1897 by Archibald Constable and Company (Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dracula, country: United Kingdom). Copyright there lasts for life plus 70 years after the death of the last surviving person named above. The last to die was Bram Stoker, in 1912, so the work entered the public domain there on 1 January 1983.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:
- SE colophon: Dracula was published in 1897 by Bram Stoker.
- Wikidata Q36184 (Bram Stoker), P570 = 1912-04-20
